# Spec — #433: Guardian state store close-out (WAL mode, `user_version` migrations, DELETE endpoint, column-policy decision)

_Milestone 0.13.0, Phase 1, task 2. Written 2026-07-12 against the current branch
(0.13.0-beta.3 baseline + merged #490). Source assessment:
[`../assessments/433.md`](../assessments/433.md) — key claims re-verified against
the working tree: no `PRAGMA journal_mode` / `user_version` anywhere in
`packages/guardian/src/` (grep-verified), `admin.ts` has list/create/rotate/
enable/disable but no DELETE (admin.ts:61-92), `state-db.ts` migrates via
sqlite_master sniffing (state-db.ts:32-68), `ownership.ts` is still an in-memory
`BoundedTtlMap`, and `rate-limit.ts` is purely in-memory._

## 0. Decisions recorded (the assessment's open calls)

- **D1 — WAL: yes.** Enable `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` at open, and extend the
  0600 discipline to the `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars (defensive `chmodSync` on any
  that exist at open time; sidecars SQLite creates later inherit the DB file's
  mode on the unix VFS, and the DB file is chmodded 0600 before any write).
- **D2 — Migrations: `PRAGMA user_version` bookkeeping, no framework.** A plain
  ordered array of migration functions plus a tiny runner. The existing
  kind-constraint rewrite (`'channel'` → `'portal'`) becomes migration v0→v1.
  Its sqlite_master sniff is retained inside the migration, which makes v0→v1
  safe on all three possible version-0 states (fresh DB / old-constraint 0.12.x
  DB / already-rewritten 0.12.x DB). The runner wraps each step **and its
  version stamp** in one transaction, and **fails closed** (throws at boot) if
  the DB's `user_version` is newer than the code's — an older guardian must
  never write a future schema.
- **D3 — `DELETE /admin/principals/:id`: implement it.** The issue's admin-CRUD
  criterion is otherwise complete-minus-delete; without it, decommissioned
  `direct` principals accumulate forever with only a disable bit, and the #486
  remote-credential provisioning flow (this milestone) needs a clean
  create→use→revoke lifecycle over curl. It is ~10 lines in `admin.ts` + one
  store accessor. Caveat documented (CHANGELOG + endpoint comment): a principal
  seeded from a `PORTAL_*_SECRET_FILE` env var is re-seeded at next guardian
  boot (`seedPortalPrincipalsFromEnv`, state-db.ts:150-161) — delete is for
  registry-managed rows (direct clients); env-seeded portal principals are
  managed by removing the addon/secret.
- **D4 — Deferred registry columns (`protocols`, `persona`, `rate_policy`):
  NOT added.** Recorded policy: **ALTER-TABLE-on-consumer under a
  `user_version` bump.** Rationale: they still have zero consumers (rate
  limiting is env-constant, `rate-limit.ts:17-27`; MCP is a seeded principal,
  `mcp.ts`; persona binding #22 has no consumer in this milestone), and adding
  them speculatively contradicts the zero-dead-code policy that trimmed them in
  0.12.0 (0.12.0 plan D1, implementation-plan.md:218). Coordination with #435
  is settled by this task's deliverable itself: the `user_version` runner is
  exactly the clean path #435 needs — if it picks cert-fingerprint mapping
  (its option b), it appends a v1→v2 migration adding a nullable
  `cert_fingerprint` column (per assessments/435.md item on `mtlsAuthStrategy`).
  The policy is recorded as a code comment next to `STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION`
  and in the issue close-out note (§ 8).
- **D5 — Phase 2 (ownership + A2A persistence): DECLINED.** The issue gates
  Phase 2 on "whether the orphan-on-restart window actually bites in practice";
  no such evidence exists, the A2A task store was never built (A2A deferred
  entirely in 0.12.0 D3), and persisting `ownership.ts` would put disk I/O on
  every session-create/permission hot path — which the issue's own principle
  forbids. Recorded in the close-out note (§ 8).

## 2. TEST-FIRST PLAN

All tests are written and committed BEFORE implementation, each observed
failing for its stated reason. Idioms to mirror (per the assessment's test
strategy, verified against the files):

- **Pure store/migration logic** → drive a raw `bun:sqlite` `Database` on a
  `mkdtempSync` temp path, never the module singleton
  (`state-db.test.ts:11-14` documents why: bun:test shares the module cache
  across files, so the singleton + import-time env read bleed between files).
- **Boot-path behavior** → spawned guardian subprocess with
  `GUARDIAN_STATE_DB_PATH` pointed at a temp file (fixture pattern:
  `proxy-direct.test.ts:48-64` `getAvailablePort`, `:149-201` spawn + health
  poll; `auth.test.ts:20-30` env-before-import).

### 2.1 `packages/guardian/src/state-db.test.ts` — REWRITE the migration describes + ADD new describes

The two existing tests (lines 45-138) inline a copy of the migration SQL; they
are **replaced** by equivalents that drive the real exported seam
`configureStateDatabase(database)` (§ 3.1), so the pinned behavior can no
longer drift from the code. Keep the existing `buildOldDb` fixture
(lines 16-36) — it is the exact 0.12.x on-disk shape.

All of these fail red first because `state-db.ts` exports neither
`configureStateDatabase` nor `STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION` (import error), and —
once the import exists — because WAL/`user_version` are not yet applied.

| Test name | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `fresh DB: creates schema, enables WAL, stamps user_version = STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION` | `new Database(tmp, {create:true})` → `configureStateDatabase(db)` → `PRAGMA journal_mode` returns `'wal'`; `PRAGMA user_version` returns `1` (`=== STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION`); `principals` table exists with the `'portal','direct'` CHECK (sqlite_master) |
| `0.12.x old-constraint DB: migrates channel→portal rows and stamps user_version 1` | `buildOldDb(tmp)` (user_version 0, `'channel'` CHECK, chan1+dir1 rows) → configure → chan1 kind `'portal'`, dir1 `'direct'`, both rows intact, user_version `1`, CHECK no longer contains `'channel'` |
| `0.12.x already-rewritten DB at user_version 0: stamped to 1 without data loss` | Build a DB with the NEW constraint + one `portal` row but user_version 0 (the upgrader state whose sqlite_master migration already ran) → configure → row intact, user_version `1` (assessment risk 2: neither re-run damage nor skip) |
| `re-running configureStateDatabase on a current DB is a no-op (idempotent re-boot)` | Configure twice on the same file (close/reopen between); rows, schema SQL, and user_version identical after the second run |
| `fails closed when user_version is newer than the code` | `PRAGMA user_version = 99` on a fresh configured DB → `expect(() => configureStateDatabase(db)).toThrow(/user_version|newer/)`; no write occurred |
| `DB file and -wal/-shm sidecars are 0600 after configuration + a write` | Configure, then `INSERT` a row through the same connection; `statSync(path).mode & 0o777 === 0o600` for the DB file and for each of `${path}-wal` / `${path}-shm` that exists; assert `${path}-wal` DOES exist (WAL mode ⇒ a write creates it — this makes the mode assertion non-vacuous) |
| `deletePrincipal removes a row and returns false for unknown ids` | Cannot use the singleton accessors (module-cache bleed) — assert at the SQL level is wrong here; instead this is covered end-to-end in § 2.3 and the accessor's contract is covered in § 2.2 via the admin API. **No unit test for `deletePrincipal` in this file** (documented decision, keeps the singleton untouched) |

## 3. File-level changes (implementation, after tests are red)

### 3.1 `packages/guardian/src/state-db.ts`

1. **Export the schema version + column policy comment:**

   ```ts
   /**
    * Bump when appending to MIGRATIONS. Column policy (#433 close-out):
    * deferred registry columns (protocols, persona, rate_policy) and #435's
    * cert_fingerprint are added by ALTER TABLE under a new user_version step
    * ONLY when their consumer ships — never speculatively.
    */
   export const STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1;
   ```

2. **`migrateKindConstraintIfNeeded` (lines 32-68):** unchanged logic, but
   REMOVE the `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` from its `exec` SQL — the migration runner
   (below) owns the transaction so the version stamp commits atomically with
   the step. Doc comment updated to say it is migration v0→v1 and why the
   sqlite_master sniff stays (it makes v0→v1 correct on all three v0 states).

3. **Migration runner (new, module-private array + exported seam):**

   ```ts
   // Ordered migrations: MIGRATIONS[n] takes user_version n → n+1.
   const MIGRATIONS: ReadonlyArray<(database: Database) => void> = [
     migrateKindConstraintIfNeeded, // v0 → v1
   ];

   function readUserVersion(database: Database): number { /* PRAGMA user_version */ }

   /**
    * Apply pragmas, versioned migrations, base schema, and the 0600
    * file-mode discipline to an open state database. Exported as the
    * unit-test seam (openDatabase() is a singleton bound to env at import
    * time and cannot be exercised in-process across test files).
    */
   export function configureStateDatabase(database: Database): void {
     database.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL'); // must run outside a transaction
     const version = readUserVersion(database);
     if (version > STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
       throw new Error(`guardian state DB user_version ${version} is newer than supported ${STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION} — refusing to open (downgrade?)`);
     }
     for (let v = version; v < STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION; v++) {
       database.exec('BEGIN');
       try {
         MIGRATIONS[v](database);
         database.exec(`PRAGMA user_version = ${v + 1}`);
         database.exec('COMMIT');
       } catch (err) {
         database.exec('ROLLBACK');
         throw err;
       }
     }
     database.exec(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS principals ( … unchanged DDL … );`);
     // 0600 discipline: DB file + any WAL sidecars that already exist.
     // Sidecars SQLite creates later inherit the DB file's mode (unix VFS).
     for (const p of [database.filename, `${database.filename}-wal`, `${database.filename}-shm`]) {
       if (existsSync(p)) chmodSync(p, 0o600);
     }
   }
   ```

   (Exact DDL string, `rowToPrincipal`, and all existing accessors unchanged.)

4. **`openDatabase()` (lines 70-92):** becomes
   `mkdirSync(dirname(DB_PATH), {recursive:true, mode:0o700})` →
   `db = new Database(DB_PATH, {create:true})` → `configureStateDatabase(db)`.
   The inline chmod/migration/CREATE lines move into `configureStateDatabase`.

5. **New accessor:**

   ```ts
   export function deletePrincipal(id: string): boolean {
     return openDatabase().query('DELETE FROM principals WHERE id = ?').run(id).changes > 0;
   }
   ```

Import style: match the file's existing style (bare `'bun:sqlite'`,
`node:` builtins; `existsSync`/`chmodSync` already imported).

- Add after the enable/disable block (before the final 404, admin.ts:87-92):

  ```ts
  const deleteMatch = url.pathname.match(/^\/admin\/principals\/([^/]+)$/);
  if (deleteMatch && req.method === 'DELETE') {
    const id = decodeURIComponent(deleteMatch[1]);
    const deleted = deletePrincipal(id);
    invalidatePrincipalCache(id);
    // NOTE: principals seeded from PORTAL_*_SECRET_FILE env are re-created at
    // next boot (seedPortalPrincipalsFromEnv) — delete is for registry-managed
    // rows; remove the addon/secret to retire an env-seeded portal principal.
    return deleted ? json(200, { deleted: id, requestId }) : json(404, { error: 'not_found', requestId });
  }
  ```

  `invalidatePrincipalCache(id)` runs unconditionally (mirrors the

## 6. Risks and how the design avoids them

1. **WAL sidecars created with default umask break the guardian-private
   invariant** (assessment risk 1). Avoided twice over: `configureStateDatabase`
   defensively chmods any existing `-wal`/`-shm` at open, and sidecars created
   later inherit the DB file's 0600 (SQLite unix VFS derives wal/shm modes from
   the main DB file, which is chmodded before any write). Proven by the § 2.1
   and § 2.2 mode assertions after a real write.
2. **Retrofitting `user_version` onto 0.12.x DBs re-runs or skips migrations**
   (assessment risk 2). Avoided by keeping the sqlite_master sniff INSIDE
   migration v0→v1: on an old-constraint DB it rewrites; on an
   already-rewritten DB it no-ops; either way the runner stamps 1. Both states
   have dedicated tests (§ 2.1 rows 2-3). The stamp commits in the same
   transaction as the step, so a crash mid-migration re-runs the (idempotent)
   step rather than skipping it.
3. **Speculative columns vs. zero-dead-code policy** (assessment risk 3).
   Resolved by decision D4 — no columns added; the versioned-migration runner
   is the coordination artifact #435 consumes.
4. **Phase 2 hot-path disk I/O** (assessment risk 4). Avoided by declining
   Phase 2 (D5) per the issue's own gating.
5. **Module-singleton test bleed** (assessment risk 5). All new unit tests
   drive raw `Database` instances via the exported `configureStateDatabase`
   seam; all boot-path tests use spawned subprocesses; nothing new touches the
   in-process singleton (the § 2.1 table explicitly declines a singleton-based
   `deletePrincipal` unit test for this reason).
6. **Future-schema downgrade corruption** (new, introduced by having versions
   at all). Fail-closed: a `user_version` above `STATE_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION`
   throws at boot before any write (§ 2.1 row 5).
7. **Complexity creep in the migration machinery.** Kept to a constant array +
   ~15-line runner — no framework, no down-migrations, no per-migration files;
   the only justification needed is the two consumers already scheduled
   (#435 v2 candidate).

## 8. Issue close-out note (draft — recorded with the issue when the milestone closes it)

> Phase 1 shipped in 0.12.0 (WS-D D1/D2b): the `principals` registry IS the
> guardian auth layer (Basic creds → cached principal), seeded from
> `PORTAL_*_SECRET_FILE`, admin CRUD on the loopback :3831 listener. This task
> completes the close-out: WAL mode + 0600 sidecar discipline,
> `PRAGMA user_version` migrations (the 0.12.0 kind-constraint rewrite is
> v0→v1), and `DELETE /admin/principals/:id`.
> Checkbox reconciliation: (a) the nonce-store criterion is satisfied vacuously
> — `replay.ts` was deleted with the HMAC transport in 0.12.0 D4 PR-3, so
> nothing existed to migrate; the rate-limit store remains in-memory as
> required. (b) "The admin UI manages rows" was consciously narrowed in 0.12.0
> to admin API + curl (no UI tab until direct ingress has users — #556).
> (c) `protocols`/`persona`/`rate_policy` columns: recorded policy is
> ALTER-TABLE-on-consumer under a `user_version` bump; #435 adds
> `cert_fingerprint` as v1→v2 only if it selects cert-identity mapping.
> (d) Phase 2 (ownership/A2A persistence) declined per the issue's own gating:
> no observed orphan-window pain, A2A deferred, and hot-path disk writes
> contradict the issue's persistence principle.
